_about: Hybrid rules. A hybrid = one PRIMARY style (owns palette, camera, caption look, sound) + at most ONE ACCENT (supplies a layer or element type). Check pairs with scripts/select_style.py --hybrid <a> <b>.
rules: Exactly one primary. The primary's palette, caption style and music mood win every conflict.
At most one accent, and it may only cover one layer: characters, environment, typography, effects, or inserts.
Shared palette lock: accent elements are recoloured into the primary palette (max 6 colours total) before use.
Shared line-weight lock: outline thickness and corner roundness come from the primary.
Shared light lock: if either layer is lit, both are lit from the same direction; flat layers get a matching drop shadow.
Shared frame-rate lock: stepped styles (stop-motion, claymation, pixel-art, hand-drawn) force the whole shot to that fps; do not mix smooth and stepped motion in one shot.
Transitions between primary and accent shots must be motivated (camera move or a cut on action), never a decorative wipe.
If after a test frame the two layers look pasted together, drop the accent. Consistency beats variety.

good_pairs.note: The only hybrid with a working engine.
